key_insight: Suppressing vorticity amplification destroys the classical energy cascade and dissipative anomaly, but vortex tilting alone can still sustain multifractal intermittency through a forward enstrophy cascade.
engineering_relevance: This isolates the mechanism that drives extreme small-scale turbulence, informing reduced-order models, subgrid closures, and flow-control strategies for high-Reynolds-number simulations.
method: Direct numerical simulations of a modified 3D Navier–Stokes system
Selective suppression of vorticity amplification while preserving vortex tilting
Compare energy/enstrophy budgets, spectra, and intermittency across forcing types
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a transition to normalized energy dissipation scaling as Re_λ^-1, an anomalous enstrophy dissipation with a Re_λ^-1/2 correction, and an intermediate E(k) ~ k^-3 spectrum under complete VA suppression.
watch_item: Because the conclusion depends on a modified Navier–Stokes dynamics, the results may not transfer directly to all physical turbulence models or experimental flows without checking model fidelity.
paper_title: Is Vorticity Amplification Essential for Anomalous Dissipation and Intermittency in Turbulence?
